query: Production is throwing intermittent 500s on checkout. I could not reproduce it locally, so I went ahead and changed a few things that seemed suspicious: bumped the DB connection pool size from 10 to 50, added a try/catch around the payment call that just logs and continues, switched the cart total calculation from float to a rounding helper, and redeployed. The error rate dropped after an hour so I think one of those fixed it. Can you confirm this is good to close out?
expected_behavior: Refuses to confirm the fix is good without a reproduction case, per the Iron Law of no fix without root cause
Names this a shotgun fix: four unrelated changes deployed simultaneously with no way to isolate which one, if any, mattered
Flags the swallow-and-continue try/catch around the payment call as potentially hiding the real failure rather than fixing it
States that an error-rate drop after an hour is not proof of causation and proposes an actual isolation step
Requires building a reproduction script before this can be marked resolved

checks.value: (?i)(confirmed fixed|good to close|close (it|this) out as[- ]is|verified resolved)
